proposal: The Mandate asks Congress to create a Title 42-style expulsion authority in Title 8, raise the credible-fear standard, codify former asylum bars and third-country transit rules, and codify Remain in Mexico and asylum cooperative agreements. It also recommends executive orders to reinstate cooperative agreements with Northern Triangle countries, restart negotiations with Mexico on Remain in Mexico, and authorize emergency rules to curtail mass migration outside Administrative Procedure Act requirements.

status_summary: As of 2026-10-17 the executive branch has acted on several parts of this objective by proclamation, order, agreement and regulation, while Congress has enacted none of the statutory changes. Proclamation 10888 and Executive Order 14165 (2025-01-20) suspended entry and asylum claims for people crossing the southern border and directed resumption of Migrant Protection Protocols (MPP); DHS published a draft environmental assessment for resuming MPP on 2025-04-25, Mexico's president said on 2025-01-22 that Mexico had not agreed to host non-Mexican asylum seekers, and no source found shows MPP operating. In RAICES v. Noem the D.C. Circuit affirmed on 2026-04-24 a district-court ruling that the proclamation cannot displace the statutory right to apply for asylum and withholding protections; rehearing was denied on 2026-07-23, the mandate was stayed on 2026-07-27, and the government filed a certiorari petition on 2026-08-24 (Mullin v. RAICES, No. 26-239), distributed for the 2026-11-06 conference. The D.C. Circuit's partial stay of 2025-08-01 let the proclamation operate as an up-front discretionary denial of asylum but not as a bypass of withholding and torture-convention procedures, per the Civil Rights Litigation Clearinghouse, and SCOTUSblog and the Center for Gender and Refugee Studies report that the asylum restriction remains in effect while review is sought. On third-country agreements, DHS published asylum cooperative agreements with Honduras (2025-07-08), Uganda (2025-09-03), Ecuador (2025-11-17), Paraguay (2025-12-23) and Belize (2026-03-12), and an advocacy center reports about 50 people transferred to Honduras between October 2025 and mid-March 2026. On asylum bars, DHS and DOJ let the public-health provisions of a 2020 security-bars rule take effect on 2025-12-31 and ratified a 2020 credible-fear rule (notice of 2025-11-19); these are regulatory steps, not the statutory changes the Mandate asks of Congress.

timeline.event: Proclamation 10888 suspends entry of people engaged in what it terms an invasion across the southern border and bars them from invoking asylum under INA section 208, with no end date until the President finds the invasion has ceased. The same day Executive Order 14165 directs DHS to resume Migrant Protection Protocols in all southern border sectors as soon as practicable, with State and Justice.

Proclamation 10888 (signed 2025-01-20) is published at 90 FR 8333 (Doc. No. 2025-01951); its asylum restriction in Sec. 2 has no fixed end date and lasts until a presidential finding that the invasion has ceased.

DHS publishes a notice of a draft programmatic environmental assessment for resuming MPP along the southern border as directed by EO 14165; the notice describes resumption as a proposed action and does not say whether operations have begun.
DHS publishes the U.S.-Honduras agreement for cooperation in examining protection requests, signed 2025-03-10 and amended by diplomatic notes of 2025-06-25.

In RAICES v. Noem (district court ruling of 2025-07-02, Judge Moss) the D.C. Circuit dissolves its administrative stay and grants the government's stay motion in part: it views the government as likely to succeed on the proclamation operating as an up-front discretionary denial of asylum, but not on removing people already in the country or on withholding and torture-convention procedures.

DHS publishes a notice that the Secretary ratified, on 2025-08-20, the interim final rule implementing bilateral and multilateral asylum cooperative agreements under the INA; the Uganda agreement is published the next day.

DHS publishes a notice that the Secretary ratified, on 2025-10-29, the 2020 final rule on credible fear and reasonable fear review and its proposed rule; the notice gives no litigation reason and says ratification does not imply the original action was invalid.

DHS and DOJ publish a final rule letting the public-health provisions of the 2020 Security Bars rule (asylum and withholding ineligibility tied to designated epidemics) take effect on 2025-12-31, while withdrawing parts of that rule that conflict with newer regulations; the agencies say current credible-fear screening is not immediately changed.

DHS publishes the U.S.-Belize agreement for cooperation regarding the examination of protection requests, following Federal Register notices of agreements with Uganda (2025-09-03), Paraguay (2025-12-23) and Ecuador (2025-11-17, signed July 2025).

A divided D.C. Circuit panel affirms the district court's summary judgment and class certification in RAICES v. Noem (174 F.4th 81): the proclamation and its guidance violate federal law insofar as they displace the statutory removal process and the right to apply for asylum or withholding of removal.

After the D.C. Circuit denied rehearing en banc on 2026-07-23 and stayed its mandate on 2026-07-27, the Solicitor General files a certiorari petition (Mullin v. Refugee and Immigrant Center for Education and Legal Services, No. 26-239); the response was filed 2026-09-23, the reply 2026-10-06, and the case was distributed on 2026-10-07 for the 2026-11-06 conference. SCOTUSblog reports the government can maintain the asylum restrictions meanwhile.

Respondents file their brief in opposition in Mullin v. RAICES (No. 26-239); amicus briefs from Iowa and other states, the Federation for American Immigration Reform, America First Legal Foundation and America's Future are filed the same day.
The government files its reply in support of the certiorari petition in No. 26-239; on 2026-10-07 the petition is distributed for the 2026-11-06 conference.

title: Restrict border asylum; restart Remain in Mexico and third-country agreements
uncertainties: Whether the asylum restriction operates today rests on SCOTUSblog and a Center for Gender and Refugee Studies litigation page, both reading the stayed mandate and the August 2025 partial stay that way; the D.C. Circuit orders themselves were not read. The Honduras transfer count (about 50, October 2025 to mid-March 2026) comes from an advocacy center's factsheet and is not confirmed by government data. The Ecuador agreement's signing date (July 2025) and Federal Register date (2025-11-17) come from the Immigration Policy Tracking Project page and a Federal Register listing, not from the notice itself. Remain in Mexico: only the order, a draft environmental assessment and Mexico's January 2025 statement were found, and two searches returned mostly 2019 to 2022 items, so absence of evidence of operations is weak. The 2020 credible-fear rule ratified in the 2025-11-19 notice and the security-bars rule are described only as the notices describe them; whether either raises the credible-fear standard as the Mandate asks was not determined. The 2026-09-21 class-certification ruling in U.T. v. Blanche comes from a Center for Gender & Refugee Studies litigation page whose footer date is 2025, so the date should be checked against the docket. Not checked: expedited asylum pathways, the Notice to Report prohibition, USCIS asylum processing holds, and the Mandate's mass-migration emergency authority (page 152). Searches run: RAICES v. Noem certiorari; MPP status 2026 (two variants); asylum cooperative agreements by country; U.T. v. Blanche status; Federal Register queries on credible fear, asylum cooperative agreements and protection-request agreements. In this review Proclamation 10888 was read in full at 90 FR 8333 and the Supreme Court docket for No. 26-239 was read in full (no entry after the 2026-10-07 distribution); the D.C. Circuit opinion and orders were not read on the court's own site, and the 2025-08-01 partial stay, the 2026-07-27 mandate stay and a 2026-07-31 district court abeyance (joint status report due 2026-10-30) were taken from the Clearinghouse case page. The reporter citation 174 F.4th 81 comes from that page and was not confirmed on a court host.
